summary:
The bullpen category is the story right now across all three live ratings — R1, R2 and R3 each sit at 100-90 (53%) over the last 14 days with matching 3-game winning streaks, a clean signal to lean on when a game's edge is coming from bullpen strength. SP is the mirror image: 45-46% across the board over 14 days, and R3's SP cell is flagged cold at -5.2pts off its season baseline. That matters today because SEA @ MIL is the slate's strongest consensus play (R1 +1.31 up to R4 +2.32 on MIL), and MIL is a proven team-when-liked winner at 62% (25-15, n=40) with strong plays running 64% for +4.0u — bullpen strength backing Milwaukee lines up with the hot category, not the cold SP one. STL @ CIN is the single biggest average delta on the board, all four ratings stacked hard on STL (-2.00 to -2.10), which is the kind of unanimous read worth full weight given trends+runs is the best-performing combo this season at 54.7%.

Where it gets trickier: TOR @ TBR and SFG @ CLE both show real spread between R1 and R3/R4 (TBR from +0.48 to +1.29, CLE from +1.17 down to +0.48), meaning the pick direction agrees but conviction doesn't — worth trusting TBR more given the team profile: TBR is 25-10 (71%) when picked, and strong plays there are money at 78% (18-5) for +22.0u, RJ's best team angle on the board bar none. HOU is the flip side — HOU shows up as a live consensus lean in LAA @ HOU, but strong-play HOU bets are ice cold at 27% (3-8, -8.0u), so any Astros lean should get sized down regardless of what the delta says. Elsewhere, NYY @ BAL and ATH @ KCR are low-conviction consensus (deltas under 1.0 across all four ratings) and don't scream confidence, while ATL @ CHW is an outright split with R3 breaking off toward ATL — skip or minimum-size that one. Zooming out, R1 and R2 are still bleeding units over the last 7 days (-15.0u and -14.0u respectively) even with plus season marks, so lean on the categories and teams, not blind rating strength, until that short-term red ink clears.
